item.description:

Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on Reformation DayThe White HouseOctober 31, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseOctober 31, 2026
From the earliest days of our Republic, prayer and faith in Almighty God have stood as the foundation of our strength, the source of our unity, and the fount of our greatness. This Reformation Day, I send my best wishes to the countless Christians across our country commemorating the Protestant Reformation and its enduring message of salvation by God’s grace through faith in Jesus Christ.
Five hundred years ago, William Tyndale—inspired by the work of Martin Luther—advanced the Protestant Reformation’s devotion to Holy Scripture through the publication of the first New Testament printed in English, shaping the language of the Bibles that would fortify the faith and resolve of America’s founding generation. The Sacred Scriptures helped form the religious convictions that formed our young Nation’s founding ideals of God-given rights and individual liberty, a spiritual inheritance we honor as we continue to reflect on 250 glorious years of American Independence. The Bible remains a cornerstone of our Nation’s character and upholds our steadfast devotion to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.
Guided by an unwavering faith in Jesus Christ, my Administration is working to restore the moral and religious foundations that have sustained our Republic for generations. As President, I will always support citizens of faith and defend their place in the public square, honoring the enduring role of our churches in strengthening families, serving communities, and preserving the core values that have anchored us across the centuries.
As Christians across our country unite in faith and fellowship this Reformation Day, I send my heartfelt prayers for a meaningful celebration and encourage each of you to draw renewed strength from God’s Word as we carry forward the blessings of faith and freedom throughout our beloved Nation.

item.title: Presidential Message on All Saints’ Day
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on All Saints’ DayThe White HouseNovember 1, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on All Saints’ DayThe White HouseNovember 1, 2026
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on All Saints’ DayThe White HouseNovember 1, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseNovember 1, 2026
On All Saints’ Day, I join Christians across our Nation in honoring the men and women through the centuries whose extraordinary lives of faithfulness reveal the great goodness and love to which human beings can aspire.
Every generation of Americans has understood the profound power of the example of a heroic and holy life, which is why the names of saints are so interwoven throughout the American landscape. We have San Francisco, California, named for Saint Francis of Assisi; San Antonio, Texas, named for Saint Anthony of Padua; St. Louis, Missouri, named for a saintly king of France; and St. Paul, Minnesota, named for the great Apostle. From Santa Monica, California, to St. Augustine, Florida, saints greet us on maps and road signs across the country.
Saints are just as present in the institutions we know and trust. Families turn to St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital when a child is gravely ill. Young Americans study at Saint John’s University, Saint Louis University, Saint Bonaventure University, and many other colleges and universities named for saints. Every March, millions of Americans celebrate Saint Patrick’s Day with parades, music, and the wearing of green.
Even our professional sports carry this legacy. When New Orleans received its National Football League franchise on November 1, 1966, the date was no accident: It was All Saints’ Day. A local businessman championed the name “Saints,” inspired by the city’s celebrated jazz anthem, “When the Saints Go Marching In.”
From sea to shining sea, these names are a constant reminder that a great civilization needs more than material success. It needs examples of goodness. It needs heroes not only of strength and achievement but also of mercy, sacrifice, humility, and love.
In the United States, we especially honor Saint Junípero Serra, who carried the Christian faith through the missions of California; Saint Elizabeth Ann Seton, who helped build Catholic education in America; Saint Katharine Drexel, who devoted her fortune and her life to educating and serving poor and impoverished communities; and Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini, who established schools, orphanages, and hospitals, putting Christian charity into action and bringing the hope of Jesus to those most in need. Countless other saints—parents, teachers, nurses, workers, missionaries, and neighbors whose names history never recorded—quietly showed what holiness can look like in ordinary life.
All Saints’ Day proclaims a truth at the heart of the Christian faith: Death does not have the final word. Christians believe that through the death and Resurrection of Jesus Christ, the grave has been conquered and eternal life has been opened to all who believe in Him. The saints are witnesses to that promise. We honor them not merely as heroes of the past but also as signs of the hope that extends to every human life and reaches beyond our earthly existence.
On this All Saints’ Day, Melania and I offer our warmest greetings to all who observe this holy feast. I will always defend the freedom of Americans to express their faith openly and without fear. May the lives of the saints renew our gratitude for our Nation’s spiritual inheritance; strengthen our resolve to love and serve one another; and inspire us to live with the faith, courage, and charity that make a people—and a nation—forever great.

The White HouseNovember 3, 2026
First Lady Melania Trump will personally bring representatives of Russia and Ukraine, two nations actively at war, together at the White House. This event represents an extraordinary moment in American history.
Mrs. Trump independently initiated engagement between the two warring nations and successfully secured a ceasefire in Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region. This achievement marks an unprecedented diplomatic initiative by an American First Lady.
First Lady Melania Trump will deliver remarks on the ceasefire in Oleshky at 11:00 am ET on Thursday, November 5, 2026, at the White House.

On Tuesday, November 3, 2026, the President signed into law:
H.R. 1744, the “United States Commission on International Religious Freedom Reauthorization Act of 2026,” which extends and authorizes annual appropriations for the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom through Fiscal Year 2028; and
H.R. 8205, the “Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026,” which reauthorizes the Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Act through Fiscal Year 2031.

item.title: First Lady Melania Trump Unites Russia and Ukraine at The White House Following Historic Ceasefire
item.description:
Office of the First LadyFirst Lady Melania Trump Unites Russia and Ukraine at The White House Following Historic CeasefireThe White HouseNovember 5, 2026

Office of the First Lady
The White HouseNovember 5, 2026
First Lady Melania Trump gathered leaders from Russia and Ukraine at the White House today. The occasion is believed to mark the first time in American history that a First Lady has personally brought representatives of two nations actively at war together to the White House for diplomacy.
The unprecedented gathering united key officials from both nations who played instrumental roles in establishing the ceasefire in Oleshky.
“Now, we must use the courage we brought to Oleshky to find common ground through a shared concern for the suffering of innocent people. Together, we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire. Let us see Oleshky as a spark in a world of darkness, capable of illuminating the best in humanity. Build a powerful flame of peace, visible to the world. Ignite hope, foster cooperation, and brighten a path toward lasting peace,” said First Lady Melania Trump.
Mrs. Trump detailed her role as Exclusive Intermediary in securing the ceasefire, facilitating the delivery of humanitarian aid to the region, and organizing the safe evacuation of nearly 800 people.
“My role as Exclusive Intermediary was memorialized in written agreements drafted and signed by both Russia and Ukraine,” the First Lady shared. “I was involved in every stage of the planning. I reviewed demining plans, aerial images, assessed roadways, and discussed evacuation routes, hospital access, vehicles, and medical resources. I was made aware of the preferred dates and timing of the operation.”
First Lady Melania Trump acknowledged, “The ceasefire in Oleshky would not be possible without President Putin and President Zelensky. Their cooperation establishes a meaningful precedent for advancing peace throughout the region.”
Ukrainian representatives presented First Lady Melania Trump with President Zelensky’s award, Ukraine’s Order of Princess Olga, First Class, the highest degree of this prestigious state honor. The award recognizes Mrs. Trump’s leadership in securing the ceasefire in Oleshky, which enabled the evacuation of 800 individuals.
Mrs. Trump concluded her historic speech by presenting the highest-ranking leaders in attendance with letters she had written to President Putin and President Zelensky.
Following her remarks, Mrs. Trump invited the distinguished guests to view two historic artifacts from the White House collection, which she personally selected as powerful symbols of peace.
The first, a late 18th-century medicine chest, was removed from the White House after British forces set the building on fire during the War of 1812. Once adversaries, the United States and Great Britain ultimately established a strong alliance
The First Lady also presented an 1899 Presentation Cup, gifted to French Ambassador M. Jules Cambon in recognition of France’s diplomatic efforts to negotiate peace and bring the Spanish-American War to an end.
Mrs. Trump’s remarks, as prepared for delivery, are below.
Oleshky, a Spark in a World of Darkness that Can Illuminate the Best in Humanity
Oleshky will forever unite the brave individuals gathered at the White House today.
We have chosen humanity over war.
Undeniably, the lives of innocent people must transcend the divisions of war.
I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace. Every significant transformation begins with a small spark.
What matters is not the modesty of this beginning, but the determination to turn it into something extraordinary.
Now, we must use the courage we brought to Oleshky to find common ground through a shared concern for the suffering of innocent people. Together, we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire.
Let us see Oleshky as a spark in a world of darkness, capable of illuminating the best in humanity. Build a powerful flame of peace, visible to the world. Ignite hope, foster cooperation, and brighten a path toward lasting peace.
I became aware of the severity of the humanitarian crisis in Oleshky in September. Recognizing the urgency, I acted immediately and directed my representative, Marc Beckman, to engage with Russia and Ukraine on my behalf, to pursue peace in Oleshky.
Both nations welcomed my participation, acknowledging that previous efforts to establish a ceasefire in the region had not succeeded.
Russia and Ukraine honored our relationship and agreed to work with me in the capacity of Exclusive Intermediary to establish a ceasefire in Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region.

Historic Donation Creates Permanent Scholarships for LSU Students From Foster Care
First Lady Melania Trump and Louisiana State University (LSU) have secured $7.2 Million to establish a permanent endowment fund supporting FOSTERING THE FUTURE scholarships for LSU students who experienced foster care.
“A great education does more than prepare someone for work life. It gives something no one can ever take away. There is nothing more powerful we can give a young person than a world-class education,” said First Lady Melania Trump.
The $7.2 Million endowment advances First Lady Melania Trump’s FOSTERING THE FUTURE initiative which provides individuals from foster care with academic scholarships to prepare them to secure an entry-level job and become financially independent.
“As adults, we have a moral obligation to our children, especially those in foster care. But, as you know, we must act to truly make a difference. The foster care community doesn’t need words,” Mrs. Trump highlighted the importance of the LSU endowment.
MMR Group committed $5 million to First Lady Melania Trump’s FOSTERING THE FUTURE, with contributions from additional LSU Foundation donors.
“Access is a top priority for LSU, because circumstances should not determine whether talent and ambition thrive. MMR Group’s visionary scholarship funding for First Lady Melania Trump’s FOSTERING THE FUTURE is transformative for youth from foster care who aspire to earn an LSU degree,” said LSU President Wade Rousse.
To celebrate the initiative, First Lady Melania Trump visited Baton Rouge for the LSU-Alabama NCAA football game, where FOSTERING THE FUTURE was prominently showcased across the stadium.
The high-visibility marketing campaign featured branded BE BEST FOSTERING THE FUTURE patches on LSU players’ jerseys, helmet decals, cheerleader uniforms during the pre-game announcement event, mascot attire, commemorative fan towels, and a limited-edition ceremonial football. SEC officials also agreed to use a First Lady Melania Trump Challenge Coin for the game’s official coin toss.
The University of Alabama is also a proud Fostering the Future partner. “Today, we have fourteen scholars at LSU and nine at Alabama. Across the country, 26 universities are supporting 100 Fostering the Future scholars this semester,” said Mrs. Trump.
In closing, First Lady Melania Trump spoke directly to America’s children and youth with experience in foster care, “To the Fostering the Future scholars here today, and throughout America: I see you. I believe in you. And I will keep working to create new opportunities with you.”
First Lady Melania Trump’s full remarks, as prepared for delivery, are provided below.
I see you. I believe in you.
At some point in a young person’s life, the world can feel like it’s moving too fast. When things are uncertain, it’s hard to know which way to go, and the future can seem out of reach.
For children navigating foster care, that feeling of drifting can feel even stronger.
Today, Louisiana State University is launching a Seven Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollar FOSTERING THE FUTURE scholarship endowment fund.
This achievement will give young people from foster care an anchor of stability, a strong educational foundation, and a chance to build a wonderful life.
Thank you, LSU, for giving the foster care community this advantage. After meeting LSU’s leadership and this remarkable community, I am not surprised by your achievement. You have united by giving young people with few resources the tools to chart their own futures.
MMR and the generous donors who made this seven million two-hundred-thousand-dollar milestone possible, know that investing in young people will create opportunities for Baton Rouge for many generations. This is very good for America.
LSU defines excellence. Your high standards start in the classroom, amplifies on the football field, and shapes America’s future leaders.
Thank you for welcoming me to Baton Rouge for one of this year’s greatest college football games: LSU versus Alabama. Both universities are part of FOSTERING THE FUTURE.
While most eyes will be on the athletes today, I encourage you to recognize LSU’s Fostering the Future scholars, who are just as remarkable. Today, we have 14 scholars at LSU and nine at Alabama. Across the country, 26 universities are supporting 100 Fostering the Future scholars this semester.

item.title: Presidential Message on Honoring the American Flag
item.description:

Briefings & Statements
The White HouseNovember 7, 2026
For nearly two and a half centuries, the American Flag has stood as the most iconic and magnificent symbol of freedom, liberty, and justice that the world has ever known. Today, we recommit ourselves to honoring our beloved Stars and Stripes by ensuring it is always treated with the utmost respect, dignity, and reverence that it so rightly deserves.
From the fateful moment the Star-Spangled Banner defiantly waved above the ramparts at Fort McHenry to the triumphant raising of the red, white, and blue atop Mount Suribachi during the Battle of Iwo Jima, throughout every generation and across every battlefield, the American Flag has shone as a radiant beacon of hope and liberty in the face of tyranny and oppression. It is the solemn duty of every American patriot to honor our Flag with unfailing loyalty, respect, and devotion—never allowing it to be dishonored or desecrated.
The United States Code, Title 4, Section 8, sets forth the proper conduct owed to our Flag. It reminds us that the Flag “represents a living country and is itself considered a living thing.” When our Flag has served its purpose and is no longer a fitting emblem for display, it should be retired in a dignified way, preferably by burning. Countless veterans service organizations, scouting groups, and patriotic Americans across our great Nation carry out these retirement ceremonies with solemn respect, and we remain grateful for their devotion to this sacred tradition.
To fully restore pride in our American Flag, last year I signed an Executive Order to prosecute those who desecrate this sacred symbol of our freedom to the fullest extent of the law. Under my leadership, anyone who defiles our Flag will face swift and unrelenting justice—including the radical rioters, agitators, and foreign nationals who despise our country, break our laws, incite violence, and seek to intimidate our citizens. This month, the Department of Veterans Affairs is launching a brand-new initiative online where Americans can access all the necessary information on how to properly respect, treat, and retire our great American Flag. Together, we will ensure the premier symbol of our great Republic is preserved for generations to come.
Today, on the Saturday before Veterans Day, we honor the sacred emblem of our beloved country—a Flag that has flown over battlefields and homesteads, been carried into combat by our bravest warriors, and been draped over the caskets of heroes who paid the ultimate price to preserve our freedom. May we continue to righteously defend the timeless values so beautifully embodied by our Stars and Stripes, and may Old Glory always be treated with the dignity and honor befitting the Flag of the greatest Nation in all of human history.

Today, I send my warmest greetings to Americans across our great Nation celebrating Diwali—the Festival of Lights.
During this special time, families gather around flickering diyas, homes shine with the warmth of ancient traditions, and countless communities glow with the beauty of a celebration thousands of years in the making. This Diwali, we observe light’s enduring triumph over the forces of darkness and honor the goodness that lives within each and every one of us—timeless values that have long enriched the great story of America.
To each American celebrating Diwali, may this joyful occasion fill your home with hope and light and your heart with the warmth of those you hold dear.

item.title: Presidential Message on National American History and Founders Month
item.description:
Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on National American History and Founders MonthThe White HouseNovember 9, 2026

Briefings & StatementsPresidential Message on National American History and Founders MonthThe White HouseNovember 9, 2026
Briefings & Statements
The White HouseNovember 9, 2026
The story of America is the greatest story of freedom in all of human history. During National American History and Founders Month, we honor the legendary patriots whose vision gave birth to our Republic; we celebrate the magnificent heritage they entrusted to us; and we pledge to carry their spirit of courage, faith, and patriotism into America’s next great chapter.
From the battlefields of the Revolution to the stunning achievements that propelled our civilization into the heavens, Americans have advanced the cause of freedom and lifted our Nation to extraordinary new heights. Their triumphs are our triumphs, their legacy is our inheritance, and their unyielding spirit of greatness courses through the veins of every American patriot—filling us with immense pride in our past and tremendous optimism for our future.
In recent decades, however, across our schools, government, and most cherished institutions, radical left-wing ideologues have worked to tarnish this indelible history and portray our past as a source of shame. At my direction, my Administration issued a report revealing that the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History—a taxpayer-funded organization entrusted with preserving our national treasures—has become a battleground in this campaign to undermine our founding principles and diminish our Nation’s extraordinary achievements.
I proudly took action to reverse this heinous betrayal of our history and restore patriotism and truth to the Smithsonian, signing an Executive Order to utilize all resources available to correct the injustices found in the report; inform visitors of the museum’s ideological bias; and ensure the Smithsonian presents an accurate, fair, and truthful understanding of American history. My Administration has restored our beloved landmarks and capital to their original beauty and moved to combat anti-American indoctrination in the classroom. In the past year, Task Force 250 has worked tirelessly to deliver the greatest, grandest, and most spectacular birthday celebration in the history of the world. Under my leadership, our national treasures are being preserved with care, our history is being presented with integrity, and our founders are once again being honored for their extraordinary contributions to human freedom.
During this National American History and Founders Month, as we celebrate our exceptional heritage and our heroic Founding Fathers, we renew our sacred promise to always honor the pioneers who built our Nation and to continue safeguarding the blessings of liberty for generations to come. I encourage all Americans—especially our Nation’s youth—to learn more about our incredible history and to draw inspiration from the noble example of those who forged our Republic. With faith in Almighty God, unwavering patriotism in our hearts, and supreme confidence in our Nation’s destiny, we affirm that the greatest chapters of the American story are yet to come.
